title: Lunit looks to bring pathology AI into drug development through US lab deal
key_facts: Korean medical AI company Lunit announced on Monday (12 Oct 2026) a partnership with U.S.-based Discovery Life Sciences, a laboratory services provider, to bring its cancer pathology software, Lunit SCOPE, into pharmaceutical research workflows.
According to Lunit, Discovery supports more than 350 active clinical trial programs and has provided biomarker services for over 2,000 trial programs in more than 25 years.

The companies will integrate Lunit SCOPE into Discovery's existing tissue processing and biomarker analysis workflows for participating pharmaceutical and biotechnology clients, rather than offering AI pathology as a standalone service.
The workflows cover tissue collection, preparation, molecular pathology and quantitative analysis.
The companies said the approach could help researchers get more consistent and reproducible tissue data across clinical and translational research programs.
Lunit did not disclose financial terms, identify participating drugmakers or say how many research programs would initially use SCOPE.
The deal comes as Lunit seeks to expand beyond cancer diagnostics into pharmaceutical research and drug development; Lunit will take part in a Discovery event in South San Francisco on Wednesday.
